title: Vendor Acceptance Playbook Sprint Kickoff
summary: Kickoff to align vendor acceptance playbook for Redwood Inference. Covered MSA/DPA redline expectations, SLA tiers, KMS/SSO integration options, data residency and pilot pricing. Agreed to three-track sprint: legal redlines, technical pilot parameters, and finance/pricing approval. Next step: Redwood to share consolidated MSA/DPA marked-up draft and pilot pricing worksheet by next Tue.
topics: MSA and DPA redlines and timelines
SLA tiering and uptime / latency targets
Privileged keying / KMS and HSM integration
Pilot scope: hosted vs dedicated, data residency requirements
Pricing approval workflow and finance signoffs
Evidence for SOC 2 / audit logs and telemetry
action_items: Avery Chen: Send consolidated marked-up MSA + DPA (combine Redwood standard with customer redlines) — due 2027-06-15
Marco Ruiz: Draft pilot runbook with test vectors, expected qps and latency SLOs for hosted and dedicated options — due 2027-06-17
Ravi Menon: Share Lumera infra diagram and KMS/HSM vendor details, list of compliance must-haves — due 2027-06-14
Ellen Wu: Provide top 5 legal must-haves for redlines (data residency, retention windows, breach notification timeline) — due 2027-06-16
Jacob Ortiz: Confirm internal finance approver and timeline for pricing approval — due 2027-06-13
next_steps: Redwood to circulate single MSA/DPA draft incorporating today's feedback
Schedule technical deep-dive (SE-led) to scope pilot perf benchmarks — target next week
Lumera to provide compliance evidence list and KMS details
Finance sync to finalize pilot pricing and committed capacity options
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-09 15:00 UTC
Duration: 53 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Dana Park (Redwood CSM), Nina Patel (Lumera Head of Platform), Jacob Ortiz (Lumera Procurement), Ravi Menon (Lumera Security Architect), Ellen Wu (Lumera Legal)

Summary (auto): Kickoff for vendor acceptance playbook and onboarding sprint. High-level asks on MSA/DPA redlines, SLA tiers, pricing approval, KMS/SSO integration.

Transcript:
[00:00:04] Avery Chen (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining — i see we have the cross-functional crew from lumera, appreciate the time. goal for today is to align on the vendor acceptance playbook steps and split into the legal, technical and finance tracks. approx 45 minute call so we'll try to be concise.
[00:00:22] Nina Patel (Lumera): thanks avery yeah should be good. we just want to make sure the m s a and d p a align to our patient-data controls, and understand the difference between hosted and dedicated for our use cases.
[00:00:35] Marco Ruiz (Redwood): quick intro from me — i'm marco, i run technical onboarding, i'll own the pilot runbook. we'll propose both hosted and dedicated profiles and a short perf bench for comparison.
[00:00:47] Jacob Ortiz (Lumera): from procurement side i'll be owning finance path and approvals. timeline wise we need final pricing to our approver by end of quarter so, uh, that constrains the sprint a bit.
[00:01:01] Avery Chen (Redwood): good call. elllen? legal?
[00:01:05] Ellen Wu (Lumera): hi — i'm elllen, sorry my mic's a bit quiet. main items: breach notification windows, data residency, retention, and the usual indemnity/liability caps. we also want to see how RBAC and SSO mapping will look, because we'll need to evidence least privilege for production access.
[00:01:23] Ravi Menon (Lumera): and i'll add that KMS/HSM flow is crucial — we can't have vendor-managed keys for certain datasets. we need to confirm whether redwood supports customer-managed keys and what the key rotation/audit looks like.
[00:01:37] Dana Park (Redwood): hey — dana from csm, i'll coordinate the onboarding checklist and admin touches, make sure we track legal signoffs and runbook items in the sprint board.
[00:01:48] Avery Chen (Redwood): great. high-level approach we usually follow: 1) legal redline sync (MSA + DPA) 2) technical pilot (3–4 week run, perf + functional checks) 3) finance/pricing sign-off. each track has owners. goal is to have a path to PROD acceptance or a narrow set of unresolved exceptions.
[00:02:07] Nina Patel (Lumera): walk me through the pilot options — hosted vs dedicated. what's the risk matrix? latency, cost, and data isolation are our top concerns.
[00:02:18] Marco Ruiz (Redwood): sure. hosted (redwood api) is fastest to start; we give region controls and can enable encryption at rest, but for absolute data isolation and customer KMS you'll likely choose dedicated or our private deployment option. dedicated gives reserved GPU pools with tenant isolation; private is full VPC/on-prem but longer lead time. performance wise dedicated's predictable throughput means lower variance for tail latency. hosted may have slightly lower unit price initially but variable latency spikes under burst.
[00:02:48] Ravi Menon (Lumera): on hosted, where are the keys? if we send PHI for inference, we need CMEK or HSM integrations. can't accept vendor-held keys for that data.
[00:02:58] Marco Ruiz (Redwood): understood — we support customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private. for hosted we have a bring-your-own-key option for certain enterprise tiers; i'll confirm exact HSM vendors we integrate with. note: for hosted, there are some architectural limits on full HSM isolation — we'll put that in the tech note.
[00:03:18] Ellen Wu (Lumera): also SLA wording — we need uptime guarantees tied to credits and also a latency SLO for API responses for our synchronous flows. do you provide per-route latency SLOs?
[00:03:30] Avery Chen (Redwood): we publish SLA tiers. typical uptime SLA is 99.9% for hosted enterprise, and we can negotiate higher for dedicated. latency SLOs are a bit more nuanced — we can commit to p95 targets for a given model and sequence length as part of the pilot; we'll include test vectors to validate.
[00:03:50] Jacob Ortiz (Lumera): will pricing for the pilot be billable usage or a fixed pilot fee? need to know to present to finance.
[00:03:58] Dana Park (Redwood): we typically do a time-limited pilot with a credit allotment that converts to a buying option. we can also propose a pilot fee that covers dedicated reservation if you want stable performance. we'll include both options in the worksheet.
[00:04:12] Nina Patel (Lumera): perf benchmarks — what metrics will you collect? we need audit logs, token-level latency, and tracing for cost attribution.
[00:04:21] Marco Ruiz (Redwood): we'll provide token-level traces, per-request latency, model version pinning, and KV cache hit rates. note the telemetry fields sometimes have slightly different names between our console and your SIEM; we'll map them.
[00:04:34] Ravi Menon (Lumera): audit logs retention — we require 13 months for security artifacts. can that be configured?
[00:04:42] Avery Chen (Redwood): yes configurable retention for audit logs on enterprise plans; we'll include options and the retention cost delta in the pricing worksheet.
[00:04:52] Ellen Wu (Lumera): redlines: we will likely ask for tighter breach notification (24 hours), restrictions on sub-processing, and stricter data deletion windows. open to discussion on liability caps if we get carve-outs on indemnity.
[00:05:06] Avery Chen (Redwood): understood. we'll try to minimize exceptions but we'll surface what's possible. i'll consolidate and return the combined draft.
[00:05:14] Jacob Ortiz (Lumera): one governance question: do you support a supplier acceptance checklist or conformance report we can add to our vendor gating?
[00:05:23] Dana Park (Redwood): yes — we can provide a conformance pack: SOC2 report pointer, architecture diagram, encryption details, SSO onboarding checklist and a short runbook that shows how we manage key rotation and access.
[00:05:34] Nina Patel (Lumera): perfect. on the technical pilot, we want to run two scenarios: realtime triage at ~50 qps with avg seq 64, and a nightly batch embedding job for 5M records — need cost guidance for both.
[00:05:48] Marco Ruiz (Redwood): we'll size both. the realtime path will show latency and p95; embedding batch will show throughput and cost per embedding. for batch we can recommend quantized model variants to reduce GPU memory and cost. i'll include expected token counts and projected egress.
[00:06:04] Ravi Menon (Lumera): data residency — some PHI must stay in eu-west-1. can you pin a region for the pilot?
[00:06:11] Avery Chen (Redwood): yes, we can pin regions for dedicated/private; hosted enterprise also supports regional tenancy for certain accounts. we'll confirm region availability and capacity.
[00:06:21] Ellen Wu (Lumera): for the MSA we will likely request specific audit rights and a right-to-audit clause for infosec assessments. is that standard?
[00:06:28] Avery Chen (Redwood): we allow contracted audit windows; we typically offer evidence (SOC2, penetration test summaries) and a process for on-site or virtual audit with notice windows. full unrestricted audit is uncommon but we can discuss scope.
[00:06:41] Jacob Ortiz (Lumera): if we need a dedicated pool reserved for production, what's the shortest lead time?
[00:06:48] Marco Ruiz (Redwood): typical lead time for reserved capacity is 4–6 weeks after contract, depends on GPU type. for pilots we sometimes use burst capacity or reserved short-term to shorten start time.
[00:06:59] Nina Patel (Lumera): can you summarize the decision points we'll need to sign off on for procurement?
[00:07:05] Avery Chen (Redwood): sure — 1) legal: MSA/DPA exceptions list (yes/no on each) 2) security: KMS and audit evidence 3) technical: pilot perf results and acceptance tests 4) finance: pricing and committed capacity option. once those are satisfied we proceed to production access.
[00:07:21] Ravi Menon (Lumera): about KMS: we have an AWS KMS and an HSM for certain keys; we need to ensure telemetry doesn't leak key material or raw PHI in logs. what logging scrub rules do you have?
[00:07:33] Marco Ruiz (Redwood): logs are scrubbed of full request and full response; we keep metadata and hashes for tracing. sensitive payloads can be redacted client-side or via a tokenization pre-step. i'll document the exact fields and default retention.
[00:07:48] Ellen Wu (Lumera): also — do you provide contractual guarantees for data deletion upon termination and for backups? sometimes vendors say they will delete but backups could persist longer.
[00:07:58] Avery Chen (Redwood): we'll include deletion timelines and backup retention in the DPA; typical windows are 30–90 days for backups depending on the plan, but we can discuss shorter windows for regulated data.
[00:08:11] Jacob Ortiz (Lumera): pricing: we need a table with pilot credits, post-pilot committed rates, and overage rates. also clarify whether embeddings are priced differently.
[00:08:21] Dana Park (Redwood): yes — we'll provide a pilot pricing worksheet with per-token and per-embedding rates, a committed capacity discount ladder, and an example cost model for your two pilot scenarios.
[00:08:33] Nina Patel (Lumera): competitor question — we run some internal evals with other providers. are there hard features you consider differentiators we should call out to finance?
[00:08:42] Avery Chen (Redwood): we position ourselves on production economics: predictable throughput, unified API across hosted/dedicated/private, and tooling for cost controls like KV caching and batching. also first-class rollouts and per-route observability.
[00:08:56] Ravi Menon (Lumera): ok. one more security ask: can you support SCIM provisioning for user onboarding?
[00:09:03] Marco Ruiz (Redwood): yes — SCIM + SAML is supported; we can map groups to RBAC roles. we'll send a sample mapping doc.
[00:09:12] Ellen Wu (Lumera): timeline ask: we need procurement signoff by 2027-07-01. is that feasible?
[00:09:19] Avery Chen (Redwood): tight but possible. we'll push to have the combined m s a/d p a and pilot pricing to you by 2027-06-15, technical deep-dive in the week of 6/21, and pilot kickoff as soon as legal clears.
[00:09:31] Jacob Ortiz (Lumera): if legal redlines are significant, what's the escalation path?
[00:09:36] Avery Chen (Redwood): legal escalation goes to our GC and commercial lead; we'll flag material exceptions early and aim to negotiate specific carve-outs.
[00:09:45] Nina Patel (Lumera): for acceptance criteria on the pilot, can you propose a short checklist? we want pass/fail gates.
[00:09:52] Marco Ruiz (Redwood): yes — proposed gates: 1) latency p95 below agreed threshold for realtime scenario 2) embedding cost per 1k within target +/- 15% 3) no critical security findings from baseline scan 4) integration of SCIM/SAML for at least two admin users.
[00:10:12] Dana Park (Redwood): we'll include those in the runbook and attach test harness scripts.
[00:10:18] Ellen Wu (Lumera): question on IP: who owns derivative outputs from the model when we send proprietary prompts?
[00:10:26] Avery Chen (Redwood): our standard is customers retain output rights; we'll confirm the clause in the MSA. if there's special IP terms, we can put them in the DPA or a schedule.
[00:10:36] Ravi Menon (Lumera): ok i will send the infra diagram and a list of the compliance artifacts we need.
[00:10:41] Jacob Ortiz (Lumera): and i'll loop in finance with the expected approval date.
[00:10:45] Avery Chen (Redwood): perfect. to keep momentum, we'll do a short technical deep-dive next week — SE-led. is Tuesday or Thursday better for your team?
[00:10:55] Nina Patel (Lumera): tuesday morning works.
[00:10:58] Dana Park (Redwood): noted — i'll send invite for Tue 2027-06-22 10:00 UTC, will confirm.
[00:11:04] Marco Ruiz (Redwood): i'll prepare two runbook variants (hosted + dedicated) and include perf test harness and a minimal dataset.
[00:11:12] Ellen Wu (Lumera): legal will do an initial pass of our redlines and prioritize the top 5 items.
[00:11:18] Ravi Menon (Lumera): i'll provide the KYM (key management) details and any onboarding constraints.
[00:11:23] Avery Chen (Redwood): great — i'll compile the MSA/DPA and pricing worksheet, send by 6/15.
[00:11:30] Jacob Ortiz (Lumera): any blockers on your side?
[00:11:33] Avery Chen (Redwood): resource-wise, no — we just need your infra and redlines to move fast.
[00:11:38] Nina Patel (Lumera): fine. one last: can you include sample contract language for regional data residency in the MSA?
[00:11:45] Dana Park (Redwood): yes — we'll add a data residency schedule with region pinning language.
[00:11:51] Ellen Wu (Lumera): thanks everyone.
[00:11:53] Avery Chen (Redwood): thanks all — quick recap then next steps.
[00:11:56] Avery Chen (Redwood): recap: Redwood sends consolidated MSA/DPA + pilot pricing worksheet by 2027-06-15; Lumera sends infra diagram and prioritized legal redlines by 6/16; schedule technical deep-dive Tue 6/22. action owners captured.
[00:12:14] Nina Patel (Lumera): noted.
[00:12:16] Jacob Ortiz (Lumera): thanks.
[00:12:18] Avery Chen (Redwood): great — we'll follow up in email. thanks everyone.

(Transcript ends; approximate auto-timestamps every 10–20s early, then summarised. Some speaker labels may be approximate.)
